newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Evergo ends morning debut at HK$1.63.
newsitem.headline: Evergo ends morning debut at HK$1.63.

text.p: Evergo China Holdings Ltd made its trading debut on Wednesday as the second most actively traded share by turnover and was at HK$1.63 per share at midday, compared with its net asset value (NAV) of HK$2.05.

"They performed very well, and it was in line with the bullish sentiment," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas. "The shares were trading at a reasonable level of about 20 percent discount to NAV."
Shares of Evergo China, a China property spinoff of Chinese Estates Holdings Ltd, hit a morning high of HK$1.74 per share after debuting at HK$1.55. It went as low as HK$1.53 per share.
Volume was 186.38 million shares worth HK$298.93 million.

"Trading at a discount to NAV is a healthy and normal practice for a property stock," said Ben Kwong, research director of Dharmala Securities. "Hong Kong property stocks are generally trading at a 10-20 percent discount to NAV."

Brokers said the recent strong debut of China property related stocks such as China Resources Beijing Land Ltd also aided sentiment. Earlier this month, shares of China Resources Beijing Land ended their trading debut at HK$4.05, up 71.6 percent from their issue price.
Brokers said they expected Evergo China to edge up a bit in the afternoon, further narrowing the trading discount to the NAV.
Last month, Chinese Estates proposed to spin off its China property development and investment businesses under a new company named Evergo China.
Chinese Estates proposed to distribute to its shareholders 25 percent of the 1.2 billion Evergo China shares on the basis of 623 Evergo China shares for every 4,000 shares of Chinese Estates held.
Evergo China's property projects, mainly in Beijing, Shanghai and southern China's Guangdong province, have been valued at HK$2.36 billion as at July 31, 1996.
